identity.title: An ALMA Survey of DCN/H<SUP>13</SUP>CN and DCO<SUP>+</SUP>/H<SUP>13</SUP>CO<SUP>+</SUP> in Protoplanetary Disks

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present ALMA observations at $\sim0.6''$ resolution of DCO$^+$, H$^{13}$CO$^+$, DCN, and H$^{13}$CN in the full disks around T Tauri stars AS 209 and IM Lup

question.value: How efficient is deuterium fractionation (DCO+/HCO+, DCN/HCN) across diverse protoplanetary disks, and how do DCN and DCO+ distributions relate to formation pathways, dust structure and the CO snowline?

evidence.quote: Constraining patterns of deuterium chemistry in protoplanetary disks is therefore useful for probing how material is inherited or reprocessed throughout the stages of star and planet formation.

bands.value: Band 6, two settings (1.1 mm and 1.4 mm)

evidence.quote: The six disks were observed during ALMA Cycle 2 (project code ) in two Band 6 spectral settings.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 1.1 mm setting: 14 SPWs (H13CN, H13CO+); 1.4 mm setting: 13 SPWs (DCN, DCO+); bandwidth-switching mode with narrow SPWs of 58.6 MHz and 0.061 MHz resolution

evidence.quote: The 1.1 mm setting, which targeted H$^{13}$CN and H$^{13}$CO$^+$ $J = 3-2$, was configured with 14 spectral windows (SPWs).
each observation used the bandwidth-switching mode, in which calibrators were observed in wider spectral windows in order to improve the signal-to-noise ratio.
The angular resolution of $\sim0.6''$ translates to physical scales of $\sim70$$80$ AU for most of the targets

what.value: Disk inclinations, position angles, systemic velocities, R_CO from CO modeling

evidence.quote: $^{a}$ Disk geometry derived from modeling millimeter/sub-millimeter CO emission

what.value: Molecular line parameters (frequency, Eu, S mu^2, partition function)

evidence.quote: taken from the Cologne Database for Molecular Spectroscopy (cite: 2001AA...370L..49M; 2005JMoSt.742..215M)
assuming the local ISM $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C ratio of 69 (cite: 1999RPPh...62..143W)

pipeline_or_manual.value: Initial calibration by ALMA/NAASC staff scripts; modified for some datasets (weights scaling, flux models) and re-run

evidence.quote: Initial flux, phase, and bandpass calibrations of the data were performed by ALMA/NAASC staff.
Subsequent data reduction and imaging were also completed with CASA 4.4.0 for the Cycle 2 data and CASA 4.5.3 for the Cycle 3 data.

flux_calibrator.value: Titan (Butler-JPL-Horizons 2012) for about half; quasars (J1924-2914, J0510+1800, J1733-1304) for others

evidence.quote: The Butler-JPL-Horizons 2012 model was used for Titan, the flux calibrator for about half the observations.
To account for the effects of ALMA’s $\sim15\%$ systematic flux calibration uncertainty

self_calibration.value: Phase self-cal of 258 GHz continuum (line-free channels of upper sideband), applied to H13CN/H13CO+ SPWs; similarly from 1.4 mm lower sideband for DCN/DCO+; IM Lup HCN from upper sideband

evidence.quote: For each disk, the 258 GHz continuum was phase self-calibrated by obtaining solutions from combining the line-free portions of the spectral windows in the upper sideband of the 1.1 mm setting.
The continuum was then imaged by CLEANing with a Briggs robust weighting parameter of 0.5.

weighting_robust.value: Continuum robust 0.5; most lines Briggs 1.0; weak lines (H13CN and DCN in MWC 480, HD 163296; H13CN in LkCa 15) Briggs 2.0

evidence.quote: Most lines were imaged and CLEANed down to a 3$\sigma$ threshold at a binned resolution of 0.5 km s$^{-1}$ using a Briggs parameter of 1.0

masking.value: Per-channel CLEAN masks; elliptical masks from disk PA, inclination and mm dust radius

evidence.quote: we used elliptical CLEAN masks based on the position angles and inclinations listed in Table [2](#tab:diskproperties) and the millimeter dust disk radii estimates
After self-calibration, the continuum was subtracted in the $uv$-plane from the SPWs containing the targeted lines.

smoothing.value: Binned to 0.5 km/s channels; CLEAN threshold 3 sigma

evidence.quote: CLEANed down to a 3$\sigma$ threshold at a binned resolution of 0.5 km s$^{-1}$

what.value: LTE reasonableness: non-LTE vs LTE H13CN column densities agree within 20% in MWC 480

evidence.quote: tested non-LTE and LTE models for H$^{13}$CN in the MWC 480 disk and found that the derived column densities agreed within 20%
the LTE approximation for their column density ratio is (cite: 2015PASP..127..266M)

unstated_but_needed: Which exact Cycle 2 project code is used for each dataset (codes blank in text)
Exact partition function values and tabulated Q_rot used
Treatment of the 15% flux scale in the elliptical-mask flux measurement beyond Monte Carlo

method.value: Re-run ALMA scripts with corrected flux models/weights in CASA, phase self-cal on continuum, apply to line SPWs

evidence.quote: the calibration scripts were modified for the 1.1 and 1.4 mm settings of AS 209, 1.4 mm setting of V4046 Sgr, 1.1 mm setting of IM Lup, and 1.1 and 1.4 mm settings of HD 163296 to scale visibility weights properly

validation.value: Compared flux models with the ALMA calibrator catalogue

evidence.quote: We verified that all other calibration scripts provided by ALMA (and available in the Archive) specify quasar flux models consistent with the ALMA calibrator catalogue.

analysis_steps.goal: Image continuum and measure dust disk radius and flux

method.value: CLEAN continuum (robust 0.5); fit ellipses to 3 sigma contours; integrate flux inside contour; uncertainty from 500 random positions

evidence.quote: fit ellipses to the 3$\sigma$ contours of the 258 GHz continuum images
measure flux densities at 500 random signal-free positions in a $25''\times25''$ continuum image, then taking the standard deviation of these measurements.

analysis_steps.goal: Image line cubes, moment maps and radial profiles

method.value: Continuum-subtract, CLEAN at 0.5 km/s with masks; moment zero maps clipped at 1 sigma; deprojected azimuthally averaged radial profiles using literature PA and inclination

evidence.quote: Figure [2](#fig:radialprofile) shows deprojected and azimuthally averaged radial profiles, which were produced from unclipped versions of the integrated intensity maps

key_parameters.value: Integration range from DCO+ emission above 3 sigma

evidence.quote: the maps were produced by summing over channels corresponding to where DCO$^+$ emission was detected above the $3\sigma$ level

validation.value: Channel maps inspected for emission outside DCO+ channels

evidence.quote: The channel maps for the other lines were inspected to check that no emission above the 3$\sigma$ level appeared in the known disk region

analysis_steps.goal: Extract integrated line fluxes and uncertainties

method.value: Elliptical aperture on cubes; 500 simulated integrated fluxes from random signal-free channels; std dev = uncertainty; detection if >3 sigma in at least 3 channels

evidence.quote: For each image cube, 500 simulated integrated flux measurements were obtained, and their standard deviation was taken to be the uncertainty in the integrated line flux.
We classify a line as detected if emission exceeding the $3\sigma$ level is observed in at least three channels
the fluxes measured with ALMA agree with Submillimeter Array observations of HCN $J=3-2$, DCO$^+$ $J = 3-2$, and DCN $J = 3-2$

analysis_steps.goal: Compute flux ratios with systematic uncertainty

method.value: 100,000 Gaussian draws per line, each scaled by a factor ~N(1,0.15); 68% interval of ratio

evidence.quote: we drew 100,000 simulated flux measurements for each line from a Gaussian distribution
we drew 100,000 simulated flux measurements for each line from a Gaussian distribution with mean and standard deviation given by the flux measurement and uncertainty provided in Table

method.value: Optically thin LTE column density ratio of DCX/H13CX at Tex 15 and 75 K, converted with 12C/13C=69; IM Lup DCN/HCN taken directly from flux ratio

evidence.quote: Assumed excitation temperatures ranged from 15 to 75 degrees
we instead computed the DCN/HCN column density ratios directly from the DCN/HCN flux density ratio
Assumed excitation temperatures ranged from 15 to 75 degrees

assumptions.value: LTE, optically thin lines, co-spatial isotopologues, negligible dust opacity, 12C/13C = 69

evidence.quote: We also neglect dust opacity when estimating the D/H ratios.

validation.value: Ratio changes only ~25% over the Tex range

evidence.quote: changing only by $\sim25\%$ in the temperature range evaluated
Subsequent data reduction and imaging were also completed with CASA 4.4.0 for the Cycle 2 data and CASA 4.5.3 for the Cycle 3 data.

used_for.value: Fit ellipses to 3 sigma continuum contours and measure centroid

evidence.quote: using the Python package SCIKIT-IMAGE (cite: scikit-image) to fit ellipses to the 3$\sigma$ contours

used_for.value: Update flux density model of J0510+1800

evidence.quote: We therefore used NRAO’s `analysisUtils` package to update the flux density model to the one listed in this table.
The DCO$^+$/H$^{13}$CO$^+$ flux ratios are comparable for the whole sample (ranging from 0.8 to 2.1)
spanning an order of magnitude from 0.2 to 2.8

findings_qualitative.value: DCN, DCO+, H13CO+ detected in all six disks; H13CN in all but IM Lup

evidence.quote: DCN, DCO$^+$, and H$^{13}$CO$^+$ are detected in all disks, and H$^{13}$CN in all but the IM Lup disk.

findings_qualitative.value: DCN is spatially compact relative to DCO+ in V4046 Sgr and HD 163296 but similar extent in AS 209 and LkCa 15

evidence.quote: Similar radial extents for DCN and DCO$^+$ emission in the AS 209 and LkCa 15 disks.

claims.hypothesis: Is deuterium fractionation efficient in diverse disks?
claims.experiment: Disk-averaged D/H from DCO+/H13CO+ and DCN/H13CN fluxes under LTE
claims.finding: Efficient fractionation comparable to other interstellar environments

evidence.quote: We find efficient deuterium fractionation for the sample

claims.hypothesis: DCN traces inner/warm disk and DCO+ outer/cold disk universally
claims.experiment: Compare radial profiles of DCN and DCO+ across six disks
claims.result: Differentiation in V4046 Sgr and HD 163296 but not AS 209 or LkCa 15
claims.finding: Dichotomy does not apply to all disks; both warm and cold DCN pathways contribute

evidence.quote: the inner disk/outer disk tracer dichotomy that was previously suggested for DCN and DCO$^+$ by the TW Hya and HD 163296 data does not apply to all disks.

claims.hypothesis: DCO+ is formed predominantly through cold H2D+ pathway rather than CH2D+
claims.experiment: Examine DCO+ radial profiles and Herbig Ae ratios
claims.result: Ring-like DCO+ common, no radially decreasing profiles; Herbig Ae ratios similar to T Tauri
claims.finding: Cold pathway dominates, warm pathway possibly secondary

evidence.quote: Our observations therefore do not provide evidence that the CH$_2$D$^+$ pathway dominates DCO$^+$ production.

claims.hypothesis: DCO+ is a robust midplane CO snowline tracer
claims.experiment: Compare DCO+ and H13CO+ gaps and rings
claims.result: Similar central dips in H13CO+ and DCO+; DCO+ extended beyond likely snowline
claims.finding: DCO+ may not reliably constrain the CO snowline

evidence.quote: the ring-like emission profiles of DCO$^+$ may not reliably constrain the location of the CO snowline.

why_this_data.value: Targets mostly chosen from disks with previous DCO+ detections in DISCS and spanning spectral types and disk morphologies

evidence.quote: the targets were mainly chosen from disks in which DCO$^+$ had previously been observed in DISCS

why_this_method.value: H13CN and H13CO+ targeted because main isotopologues expected to be optically thick

evidence.quote: H$^{13}$CN and H$^{13}$CO$^+$ were targeted rather than the main isotopologues because the corresponding transitions of the latter are expected to be optically thick in disks

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: CH2D+ pathway for DCO+ (Favre et al. 2015) not supported by observed central gaps

evidence.quote: the DCO$^+$ emission features prominent central gaps where DCN is brightest

limitations_admitted.value: Assumes co-spatial isotopologues, LTE, ISM 12C/13C; selection bias toward DCO+-bright massive disks; resolution limits morphology classification

evidence.quote: inferences about deuterium fractionation based on optically thin isotopologues require the assumption that the $^{12}$C and $^{13}$C isotopologues are co-spatial.
The classification of emission morphologies is dependent on the spatial resolution

referee_caveats_inferred: Disk-averaged D/H mixes regions with different local ratios
HCN optical depth for IM Lup assumed thin
Single excitation temperature for the whole disk

evidence.quote: all other calibration scripts provided by ALMA (and available in the Archive)
